</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">The Alcar
    Group, Inc.</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In April 2003, Hyperion acquired substantially all of the assets
    and assumed certain liabilities of The Alcar Group, Inc., a
    strategic financial modeling software provider based in Skokie,
    Illinois. This acquisition was accounted for using the purchase
    method of accounting in accordance with SFAS&#160;141.
    Hyperion&#146;s consolidated statements of operations include
    the results of Alcar from the date of acquisition.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Alcar provides strategic financial modeling solutions used by
    senior managers in corporate finance and business development,
    treasury, strategy, and risk management. Alcar&#146;s solution
    is used to analyze and model the financial impact of critical
    business decisions, such as mergers, acquisitions, divestitures,
    treasury activities, capital allocation, and debt restructuring.
    Alcar&#146;s strategic modeling solution is an adjacent
    application that fills a customer need and complements our
    Business Performance Management offering. This acquisition has
    resulted in greater integration of strategic financial modeling
    in the Business Performance Management process.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The aggregate purchase price for the net assets of Alcar was
    cash of $6.5&#160;million, $0.5&#160;million of which was
    deferred and was paid in fiscal 2004. Of the $6.5&#160;million
    purchase price, approximately $0.1&#160;million was allocated to
    the net liabilities assumed, approximately $2.3&#160;million was
    allocated to acquired technologies, which are being amortized
    over three years, and approximately $4.3&#160;million was
    allocated to goodwill. There was no IPR&#38;D expense incurred
    as a result of this acquisition. In fiscal years 2005 and 2004,
    Hyperion made additional performance payments to the
    shareholders of Alcar for achieving certain revenue targets.
    These payments totaled $1.1&#160;million and $0.4&#160;million
    for fiscal years 2005 and 2004, respectively, and were recorded
    as additional goodwill.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Auction rate securities are securities that are structured with
    short-term interest rate reset dates of generally less than
    ninety days but with maturities in excess of ninety days. At the
    end of the reset period, which occurs every seven to thirty-five
    days, investors can sell or continue to hold the securities at
    par. Variable rate demand notes are long-term tax-exempt bonds
    that bear floating interest rates that are tied to a money
    market rate, and provide investors the option to tender or put
    securities at par on seven days notice, or in some cases within
    a day&#146;s notice. Auction rate securities and variable rate
    demand notes are classified in the table below based on their
    legal stated maturity dates.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Even though certain stated maturity dates of these investments
    exceed one year beyond the balance sheet dates, we have
    classified all marketable investments as short-term investments.
    In accordance with Accounting Research
    Bulletin&#160;No.&#160;43, Chapter&#160;3A, &#147;Working
    Capital-Current Assets and Current Liabilities,&#148; we view
    our
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">available-for-sale</FONT>
    portfolio as available for use in our current operations. Based
    upon historical experience in the financial markets as well as
    our specific experience with these investments, we believe there
    is a reasonable expectation of completing a successful auction
    within the subsequent twelve-month period. During our history of
    investing in these securities, we have not been unable to sell
    our holdings of these investments. Accordingly, we believe that
    the risk of non-redemption of these investments within a year to
    be minimal.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Gross realized gains and losses from the sale of investments
    were not material for fiscal 2006, 2005, and 2004.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We regularly review all of our investments for
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">other-than-temporary</FONT>
    declines in fair value. Our review includes the consideration of
    the cause of the impairment including the creditworthiness of
    the security issuers, the number of securities in an unrealized
    loss position, as well as the severity and duration of the
    unrealized losses. When we determine that the decline in fair
    value of an investment below our accounting basis is
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">other-than-temporary,</FONT>
    we reduce the carrying value of the securities we hold and
    record a loss in the amount of such decline. No such reductions
    have been required during fiscal 2006, 2005, or 2004.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

    <B><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">PROPERTY AND
    EQUIPMENT</FONT></B>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Property and equipment are recorded at cost, less accumulated
    depreciation and amortization. Upon disposal of property and
    equipment, the cost and accumulated depreciation or amortization
    of the assets are removed from the accounting records, and the
    related gain or loss on disposal is recognized in the results of
    operations. Depreciation is generally computed using the
    straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the
    applicable assets. Leasehold improvements are amortized over the
    lesser of the remaining term of the lease or the useful life of
    the improvements. Repairs and maintenance expenditures, which
    are not considered improvements and do not extend the useful
    lives of the assets, are expensed as incurred.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During fiscal 2006, 2005, and 2004, Hyperion capitalized product
    development costs of approximately $6.7&#160;million,
    $5.8&#160;million, and $2.2&#160;million, respectively.
    Amortization of intangible assets totaled $13.2&#160;million,
    $12.9&#160;million, and $9.3&#160;million, of which
    $3.1&#160;million, $2.7&#160;million, and $2.3&#160;million
    related to product development costs, for fiscal 2006, 2005, and
    2004, respectively. Product development costs and acquired
    technologies are generally amortized over three years, and other
    intangibles are amortized over periods between one and seven
    years.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of June&#160;30, 2006, Hyperion has approximately
    $29.0&#160;million of U.S.&#160;federal net operating loss
    carryforwards, which begin to expire in 2022, and
    $4.0&#160;million of state net operating loss carryforwards,
    which begin to expire between 2007 and 2022. As of June&#160;30,
    2005, Hyperion had approximately $29.0&#160;million and
    $6.0&#160;million of federal and state net operating loss
    carryforwards, respectively. In addition, as of June&#160;30,
    2006, and June&#160;30, 2005, Hyperion&#146;s
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">non-U.S.&#160;net</FONT>
    operating loss carryforwards for income tax purposes were
    approximately $30.5&#160;million and $34.5&#160;million,
    respectively. For the
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">non-U.S.&#160;net</FONT>
    operating loss carryforwards, Hyperion believes that based upon
    the weight of available evidence, it is likely that the deferred
    tax assets will not be fully recognized and has, therefore,
    recorded a valuation allowance of $8.8&#160;million and
    $10.4&#160;million as of June&#160;30, 2006, and June&#160;30,
    2005, respectively.

    In March 1998, Hyperion issued $100.0&#160;million of
    4.5%&#160;convertible subordinated notes, due March 2005. The
    notes were subordinated to all existing and future senior debt
    and were convertible into shares of Hyperion&#146;s common stock
    at a conversion price (stock split-adjusted) of $37.57&#160;per
    share. The notes were also redeemable at the option of Hyperion,
    in whole or in part, at any time on or after March&#160;20,
    2001, at 104.5% of the principal amount initially, and
    thereafter at prices declining to 100% at maturity, in each case
    together with accrued interest. Each holder of the notes had the
    right, subject to certain conditions and restrictions, to

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    require Hyperion to offer to repurchase all outstanding notes,
    in whole or in part, owned by such holder, at specified
    repurchase prices together with accrued interest upon the
    occurrence of certain events. Hyperion incurred
    $3.3&#160;million of costs in connection with the issuance of
    the notes, which were deferred and included in other assets.
    These finance costs were being recognized as interest expense
    over the term of the notes using the straight-line method, which
    approximated the effective interest method. Interest on the
    notes began accruing March&#160;16, 1998 and was payable
    semi-annually on March 15 and September&#160;15.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During fiscal 2004, Hyperion redeemed its outstanding
    convertible subordinated notes with face values totaling
    $50.0&#160;million. This redemption resulted in the recognition
    of a loss of $0.9&#160;million in fiscal 2004, which was
    comprised of the 1.286% redemption premium paid as well as the
    write-off of associated deferred issuance costs.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Hyperion&#146;s President and Chief Executive Officer serves on
    the Board of Directors of Citrix Systems, Inc. In fiscal 2006,
    Citrix purchased approximately $1.7&#160;million of software,
    maintenance, and services from Hyperion for their System 9
    implementation. As of June&#160;30, 2006, all amounts due from
    Citrix related to these sales had been paid.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    A member of Hyperion&#146;s Board of Directors serves on the
    Board of Directors of Frontrange Solutions. In fiscal 2006,
    Frontrange Solutions purchased approximately $0.1&#160;million
    of services from Hyperion. As of June&#160;30, 2006, all amounts
    due from Frontrange Solutions related to these sales had been
    paid.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    A member of Hyperion&#146;s Board of Directors serves on the
    Board of Directors of Gartner, Inc. In fiscal 2006, Gartner,
    Inc. purchased approximately $0.7&#160;million of software,
    maintenance, and services from Hyperion. As of June&#160;30,
    2006, all amounts due from Gartner related to these sales had
    been paid. Hyperion purchased approximately $0.5&#160;million
    from Gartner. As of June&#160;30, 2006, all amounts due to
    Gartner had been paid.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">Lease
    Commitments</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Hyperion leases office and research facilities and certain
    computer and other equipment under operating and capital lease
    agreements expiring at various dates through 2014. In addition
    to base rent, Hyperion is responsible for certain taxes,
    utilities, and maintenance costs. Additionally, many leases
    include rentals based upon fixed dollar increases in rent per
    square foot, fixed percentage increases, changes in the Consumer
    Price Index, or the fair market rental value of the property,
    and several leases contain options for renewal. Hyperion
    subleases some of its facilities to third-party tenants. These
    subleases expire at various dates through 2010.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>    <B>[2]</B>&#160;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">    Represents remaining payments under capital leases of computer
    equipment, including $0.1&#160;million of imputed interest.
</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="line-height: 3pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>    <B>[3]</B>&#160;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">    Represents amounts associated with agreements that are
    enforceable, legally binding, and specify terms, including:
    fixed or minimum quantities to be purchased; fixed, minimum, or
    variable price provisions; and the approximate timing of the
    payment.
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We recognize rental expense on a straight-line basis over the
    term of the lease. Rental expense for fiscal 2006, 2005, and
    2004 under all lease agreements was $16.6&#160;million,
    $22.8&#160;million, and $15.4&#160;million, respectively.
    Sublease income was $7.0&#160;million, $3.3&#160;million, and
    $3.0&#160;million for fiscal 2006, 2005, and 2004, respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">Contingencies</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In December 2004, Hyperion filed an action against OutlookSoft
    Corporation (&#147;OutlookSoft&#148;) in Federal District Court
    for the Eastern District of Texas, charging that OutlookSoft is
    infringing two Hyperion patents relating to its financial
    consolidation, reporting, and analysis applications, Hyperion
    Financial Management and Hyperion Enterprise. Hyperion is asking
    for damages for past infringement, including treble damages for
    willful infringement, and an injunction against further
    infringement. In January 2005, OutlookSoft answered the
    complaint by denying infringement and challenging the validity
    and enforceability of the Hyperion patents. OutlookSoft also
    filed counterclaims alleging that Hyperion infringed two of its
    patents, asked for damages for past infringement, including
    treble damages for willful infringement, and an injunction
    against further infringement. On August&#160;28, 2006, the court
    granted Hyperion&#146;s Motion For Summary Judgement dismissing
    all OutlookSoft counterclaims. Trial is scheduled to begin on
    September&#160;11, 2006. We intend to vigorously pursue the
    protection of our intellectual property. As we are unable to
    predict the outcome of the litigation and presently cannot
    estimate any possible gain at this time, we have not recorded
    any estimated gain in our consolidated financial statements.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In November 2004, Hyperion filed a declaratory judgment action
    in Federal District Court for the Northern District of
    California against HyperRoll, Inc. (&#147;HyperRoll&#148;) to
    establish that Hyperion did not infringe any of HyperRoll&#146;s
    patents. In January 2005, HyperRoll Israel Ltd., a HyperRoll
    subsidiary, filed an action in Federal District Court for the
    Eastern District of Texas against Hyperion claiming that
    Hyperion infringed two HyperRoll patents relating to our
    multidimensional database product, Essbase, claiming violations
    of the Latham Act regarding claims made about our products, and
    a claim for patent mis-marking. On May&#160;4, 2005, the Federal
    District Court for the Eastern District of Texas granted
    Hyperion&#146;s Motion of Transfer Action to the Federal
    District Court for the Northern District of California and,
    presently, the case is consolidated with Hyperion&#146;s
    Declaratory Judgment action. Hyperion will vigorously defend the
    claims. We are unable to predict the outcome of the litigation
    and, because we cannot estimate any possible loss at this time,
    we have not recorded any estimated loss in our consolidated
    financial statements.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">Stock
    Repurchases</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On May&#160;20, 2004, Hyperion&#146;s Board of Directors
    authorized the company to repurchase up to $75.0&#160;million of
    its common stock. All authorized funds under this repurchase
    program were spent by the end of fiscal 2005. On May&#160;16,
    2005, the Board of Directors authorized us to repurchase up to
    an additional $125.0&#160;million. All authorized funds under
    this repurchase program were spent by the end of fiscal 2006. On
    April&#160;20, 2006, upon completion of the May 2005 repurchase
    plan, the Board of Directors approved a third stock repurchase
    program of $100.0&#160;million. As of June&#160;30, 2006, the
    remaining authorized amount for stock repurchases under the
    program was $65.0&#160;million. All shares repurchased under
    these repurchase programs were retired at the time of repurchase.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In fiscal 2001, Hyperion repurchased and held in treasury a
    total of 2,084,000&#160;shares of its common stock for a total
    cost of $23.8&#160;million. In fiscal 2004, Hyperion reissued
    823,000&#160;shares of treasury stock in connection with
    employee stock option exercises and employee stock purchases. As
    of June&#160;30, 2006, Hyperion holds no shares of treasury
    stock.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">Stock Option
    Plans</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of June&#160;30, 2006, Hyperion had an aggregate of
    11.1&#160;million shares reserved for future issuance under its
    equity plans. The equity plans provide for the issuance of
    common shares pursuant to stock option exercises, issuances of
    restricted stock awards, restricted stock units, and other
    equity-based awards. There were 2.3&#160;million shares
    available for grant under the equity plans as of June&#160;30,
    2006. Under the equity plans, stock options, restricted stock
    awards, and restricted stock units can be issued to employees
    and to non-employee directors.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Stock options are generally granted to employees, officers, and
    non-employee directors under the equity plans with exercise
    prices equal to the fair market value of the common stock on the
    date of grant and generally vest over a period of four years.
    Options granted that have been under the Hyperion&#146;s equity
    plans have maximum terms ranging from six to ten years from the
    date of grant. Options currently issued under Hyperion&#146;s
    2004 Equity Incentive Plan, as amended, have expiration dates no
    greater than six years from date of grant. Certain options
    provide for accelerated vesting upon certain events, including
    an employee&#146;s involuntary termination, as defined in the
    plan, within eighteen months following a change in control of
    Hyperion.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The aggregate intrinsic value is the sum of the amounts by which
    the quoted market price of our stock exceeded the exercise price
    of the options at June&#160;30, 2006, for those options for
    which the quoted market price was in excess of the exercise
    price
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">(&#147;in-the-money</FONT>
    options&#148;). The weighted average grant-date fair value of
    options granted during fiscal 2006, 2005, and 2004 was $12.81,
    $11.75, and $10.59, respectively. The total intrinsic value of
    options exercised during fiscal 2006, 2005, and 2004 was
    $32.1&#160;million, $51.4&#160;million, and $44.1&#160;million,
    respectively. The total cash received from employees as a result
    of stock option exercises was $36.1&#160;million,
    $56.1&#160;million, and $52.0&#160;million for fiscal 2006,
    2005, and 2004, respectively. In connection with these
    exercises, Hyperion realized tax benefits of $9.2&#160;million,
    $11.2&#160;million, and $15.5&#160;million for fiscal 2006,
    2005, and 2004, respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On November&#160;21, 2005, the Board of Directors approved a
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">three-for-two</FONT>
    stock dividend of our common stock payable on December&#160;19,
    2005, to stockholders of record as of December&#160;1, 2005. On
    December&#160;19, 2005, the number of employee stock options
    that were issued and outstanding under all existing equity
    compensation plans and their corresponding exercise prices were
    adjusted for the effect of the stock dividend. The antidilution
    provisions of the 2004 Equity Incentive Plan, as amended, did
    not require these modifications to be made on the options issued
    under this plan. Accordingly, during fiscal 2006, we recorded
    incremental compensation expense of $2.0&#160;million resulting
    from the modifications of 2.6&#160;million stock options that
    were issued and outstanding under the 2004 Equity Incentive Plan
    and were held by approximately 1,000 employees. At June&#160;30,
    2006, the unrecognized compensation cost associated with these
    modified stock options was $8.5&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of June&#160;30, 2006, the total unrecognized compensation
    cost related to all unvested options not yet recognized is
    $49.4&#160;million, including the $8.5&#160;million compensation
    charge relating to the stock split modification, and is expected
    to be recognized over the weighted average period of
    2.7&#160;years.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">Restricted
    Stock Awards</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Hyperion grants restricted stock awards to certain of its
    employees, officers, and non-employee directors for nominal
    consideration. Restricted stock awards generally vest over a
    three to four-year period on the anniversary of the date of
    issuance, and some grants may vest earlier based upon the
    achievement of specific performance-based objectives set by the
    Board of Directors and through acceleration clauses in officer
    employment agreements.
</DIV>

    <BR>
    <FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">66
    </FONT>
</DIV><!-- END LOGICAL PAGE -->

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">Restricted
    Stock Units</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During fiscal 2006, Hyperion started the issuance of restricted
    stock unit awards as an additional form of equity compensation
    to its employees and officers, pursuant to Hyperion&#146;s
    stockholder-approved 2004 Equity Incentive Plan. Restricted
    stock units generally vest over a four-year period and unvested
    restricted stock units are forfeited and cancelled as of the
    date that employment terminates. Restricted stock units are
    settled in shares of Hyperion&#146;s common stock upon vesting.
</DIV>

<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="width: 86%; margin-left: 7%"><!-- BEGIN LOGICAL PAGE -->

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">Employee Stock
    Purchase Plan</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Hyperion sponsors an employee stock purchase plan
    (&#147;ESPP&#148;) that is qualified under Section&#160;423 of
    the Internal Revenue Code. Under the ESPP, substantially all
    employees may purchase Hyperion common stock through payroll
    deductions at a price equal to 85% of the lower of the fair
    market value at the beginning or end of each six-month offering
    period. Stock purchases under the ESPP are limited to 10% of an
    employee&#146;s eligible compensation, 1,000&#160;shares per
    offering period, and a fair market value of $25,000 in any plan
    year. In fiscal 2006, 2005, and 2004, approximately
    0.5&#160;million, 0.5&#160;million, and 0.6&#160;million shares,
    respectively, were issued under the ESPP. At June&#160;30, 2006,
    approximately 1.5&#160;million shares were reserved for future
    issuance under the ESPP. The total cash received from employees
    as a result of employee stock purchases was $13.1&#160;million,
    $11.8&#160;million, and $9.9&#160;million for fiscal 2006, 2005,
    and 2004, respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">Employee
    Savings Plans</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Hyperion maintains an employee savings plan that qualifies as a
    cash or deferred salary arrangement under Section&#160;401(k) of
    the Internal Revenue Code. Under the plan, participating
    U.S.&#160;employees may defer up to 15% of their pre-tax
    compensation, but generally not more than $15,000 in calendar
    year 2006 and $14,000 in calendar year 2005. Hyperion
    contributes to the plan quarterly, up to a maximum of
    $500&#160;per quarter, per participant. Similar savings plans
    are maintained with respect to certain
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">non-U.S.&#160;employees.</FONT>
    In fiscal 2006, 2005, and 2004, Hyperion contributed
    $6.8&#160;million, $6.6&#160;million, and $6.2&#160;million,
    respectively, to the savings plans.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

<TR>
    <TD width="4%"></TD>
    <TD width="96%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">16.&#160;&#160;</FONT></B>
</TD>
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">STOCKHOLDER
    RIGHTS PLAN</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In June 1998, Hyperion adopted a stockholder rights plan in
    which preferred stock purchase rights were distributed as a
    rights dividend at the rate of one right for each share of
    common stock held as of the close of business on July&#160;3,
    1998. The rights plan is designed to prevent an acquirer from
    gaining control of Hyperion without offering a fair price to all
    of Hyperion&#146;s stockholders. The plan is intended to protect
    the interests of stockholders in the event Hyperion is
    confronted in the future with coercive or unfair takeover
    tactics.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Each right will entitle holders of Hyperion&#146;s common stock
    to buy 2/3000 of a share of Series&#160;A Junior Participating
    Preferred Stock of Hyperion at an exercise price of
    $250&#160;per 1/1000 of a preferred share. Generally, the rights
    will be exercisable only if a person or group acquires more than
    15% of the common stock or announces a tender or exchange offer
    which would result in its ownership of 15% or more of the common
    stock, or a person owning 10% or more of the common stock is
    determined by the board to be an adverse person, as defined in
    the rights plan. Under the rights plan, the ownership, tender
    offer, and exchange offer thresholds of 15% increase to 25% for
    certain grandfathered stockholders and approximately 20.5% for
    one stockholder that held approximately 19.5% of Hyperion&#146;s
    issued and outstanding stock on July&#160;3, 1998.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    If any person or group becomes the beneficial owner of 15% or
    more of the common stock, each right not owned by such person or
    related parties will entitle its holder to purchase, at the then
    current exercise price of the right, common stock of Hyperion
    having a value of twice the right&#146;s exercise price (or, in
    certain circumstances, a combination of cash, property, common
    stock, or other securities or a reduction in the exercise price
    having an aggregate value equal to the value of the common stock
    otherwise purchasable). After the occurrence of a triggering
    event and before any person or affiliated group becomes the
    owner of 50% or more of the then outstanding common stock,
    Hyperion may also exchange one share of common stock for each
    right outstanding. In addition, if Hyperion is involved in a
    merger or other business combination transaction with another
    person in which its common stock is changed or converted, or
    sells or transfers more than 50% of its assets or earning power
    to another person, each right that has not previously been
    exercised will entitle its holder to purchase, at the then
    current exercise price of the right, shares of common stock of
    such other person having a value of twice the right&#146;s
    exercise price.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Hyperion can redeem the rights at $0.01&#160;per right prior to
    the date the ownership thresholds are passed. The rights will
    expire on July&#160;3, 2008, unless earlier redeemed or
    exchanged.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    <FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">68
    </FONT>
</DIV><!-- END LOGICAL PAGE -->

<TR valign="top">
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">17.&#160;&#160;</FONT></B>
</TD>
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">RESTRUCTURING AND
    OTHER CHARGES</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During fiscal 2006, we received notification of departure from a
    tenant who decided not to renew its sublease contract on our
    leased facility in Egham, United Kingdom. The sublease with our
    tenant expires on August&#160;29, 2006. Our original lease
    contract with the main landlord on the facility expires on
    March&#160;13, 2021, with an option to exit the lease five years
    earlier on March&#160;13, 2016. During the fourth quarter of
    fiscal 2006, we determined that we would not utilize the space
    that the subtenant will vacate at the end of August 2006 through
    the remainder of our lease term. Accordingly, we recorded a
    restructuring charge of $3.6&#160;million during the fourth
    quarter ended June&#160;30, 2006. These restructuring costs were
    accounted for under Statement of Financial Accounting Standards
    No.&#160;146, &#147;Accounting for Costs Associated with Exit or
    Disposal Activities&#148; (&#147;SFAS&#160;146&#148;) and are
    included as a charge to Hyperion&#146;s results of operations.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In the second quarter of fiscal 2006, management approved and
    initiated plans to eliminate certain duplicative activities
    associated with the customer support and engineering
    organizations. We recorded a restructuring charge of
    $0.7&#160;million for employee severance benefits and
    $0.1&#160;million for facility closure costs in fiscal 2006.
    These restructuring costs were accounted for under SFAS&#160;146
    and are included as a charge to Hyperion&#146;s results of
    operations. Through June&#160;30, 2006, we paid
    $0.5&#160;million on this restructuring plan. Future cash
    payments related to this restructuring plan are expected to be
    substantially completed by December&#160;31, 2006.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During fiscal 2005, we vacated our facilities in Sunnyvale and
    San&#160;Francisco, California. This resulted in a restructuring
    charge in fiscal 2005 of approximately $6.1&#160;million. These
    restructuring costs, net of adjustments, were accounted for
    under SFAS&#160;146. All amounts under this restructuring plan
    were substantially paid as of June&#160;30, 2005.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2004, we signed an engineering
    consulting agreement with a consulting firm based in Bangalore,
    India, in an effort to increase our offshore development
    capacity and capability. As a result of this initiative, in July
    2004, we reduced our
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">U.S.-based</FONT>
    development staff by approximately 50 employees, or
    approximately 10% of our development headcount, and, under
    SFAS&#160;146, recorded a restructuring charge in fiscal 2005 of
    approximately $1.0&#160;million. This restructuring charge
    consisted of severance and related benefits costs. All amounts
    under this restructuring plan were substantially paid as of
    June&#160;30, 2005.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In connection with the acquisition of Brio in October 2003,
    Hyperion recorded $36.1&#160;million of restructuring costs in
    connection with exiting certain pre-acquisition activities of
    Brio, including $4.8&#160;million of employee severance costs,
    $26.6&#160;million of facility closure costs, and
    $4.7&#160;million of asset impairments related to the facility
    closures. These costs have been recognized as liabilities
    assumed in the purchase business combination in accordance with
    Emerging Issues Task Force Issue
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;95-3,</FONT>
    &#147;Recognition of Liabilities in Connection with a Purchase
    Business Combination&#148; (&#147;EITF&#160;95-3&#148;). In
    fiscal year 2005, Hyperion adjusted the restructuring charges
    recorded in fiscal 2004 by $(0.5)&#160;million, which is
    included as a credit to Hyperion&#146;s results of operations
    and resulted from a change in the estimate of sublease income
    primarily related to the Santa&#160;Clara, California facility.
    Future cash payments related to the Brio restructuring plan are
    expected to be substantially completed by the end of June 2010.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In June 2001, Hyperion announced a corporate restructuring plan
    designed to bring costs more in line with revenues and
    strengthen the financial performance of the company, which
    resulted in a reduction of the workforce by approximately 300,
    or 12% of worldwide headcount. Employee groups impacted by the
    restructuring included personnel involved in corporate services,
    product business units, sales, and customer support. In
    addition, Hyperion consolidated some of its facilities and
    exited other facilities. In June 2001, the total amount recorded
    as restructuring and other charges was $42.8&#160;million and
    was accounted for under Emerging Issues Task Force
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;94-3,</FONT>
    &#147;Liability Recognition for Certain Employee Termination
    Benefits and Other Costs to Exit an Activity (including Certain
    Costs Incurred in a Restructuring)&#148;
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">(&#147;EITF&#160;94-3&#148;),</FONT>
    which was subsequently superseded by SFAS&#160;146. In fiscal
    years 2005, 2004, 2003, and 2002, Hyperion adjusted the
    restructuring charges recorded in fiscal 2001 by
    $(0.6)&#160;million, $0.6&#160;million, $0.8&#160;million, and
    $0.1&#160;million, respectively. These adjustments resulted
    primarily from a change to the estimate of sublease income
    related to our facility exit costs and did not represent new
    restructuring activities. Future cash payments related to this
    restructuring plan are expected to be made through September
    2008.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    <FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">69

    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica">CONTROLS AND

</TD>

<DIV style="margin-top: 4pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 4%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <B>EVALUATION OF DISCLOSURE CONTROLS AND
    PROCEDURES.</B>&#160;&#160;Our management, with the
    participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial
    Officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure
    controls and procedures (as such term is defined in
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">Rules&#160;13a-15(e)</FONT>
    and
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">15d-15(e)</FONT>
    under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the
    &#147;Exchange Act&#148;), as of the end of the period covered
    by this report. Based on such evaluation, our Chief Executive
    Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that, as of
    the end of such period, our disclosure controls and procedures
    are effective.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 4pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 4%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <B>MANAGEMENT&#146;S REPORT ON INTERNAL CONTROL OVER FINANCIAL
    REPORTING.</B>&#160;&#160;Our management is responsible for
    establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over
    financial reporting, as such term is defined in Exchange Act
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">Rules&#160;13a-15(f)</FONT>
    and
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">15d-15(f).</FONT>
    Under the supervision and with the participation of our
    management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief
    Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of the
    effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting
    as of June&#160;30, 2006 based on the framework in <I>Internal
    Control&#160;&#150; Integrated Framework </I>issued by the
    Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway
    Commission. Based on our evaluation under the framework in
    <I>Internal Control&#160;&#150; Integrated Framework</I>, our
    management concluded that our internal control over financial
    reporting was effective as of June&#160;30, 2006. Our
    management&#146;s assessment of the effectiveness of our
    internal control over financial reporting as of June&#160;30,
    2006 has been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an
    independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in
    their report included at Item&#160;8 in this Annual Report on
    Form <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">10-K.</FONT>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 4pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 4%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 9pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <B>CHANGE IN INTERNAL CONTROL OVER FINANCIAL
    REPORTING.</B>&#160;&#160;There have not been any changes in our
    internal control over financial reporting (as such term is
    defined in
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">Rules&#160;13a-15(f)</FONT>
    and
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">15d-15(f)</FONT>
    under the Exchange Act) during the fourth fiscal quarter that
    have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially
    affect, our internal control over financial reporting.
</DIV>
